title: The deploy engine: build at the landed sha, replace atomically, probe health, keep the previous receipt
description:
SPIDR child of task-04b3ce7e349743c2a156d32ee5550ba5 (architect-fa3a3e17, 2026-09-05), which measured over the file cap. dependsOn task-3706b7e7bb8741d88105f42c25166ea0 for the infrastructure files it builds from.

WHY THIS ROW EXISTS. The parent publishes TWO command kinds (`deployment.set_target`, `deployment.deploy`) AND owns the deploy effect. Publishing one command kind on this board is measured at 13 forced edits; two is more, and the engine is another eight files. This row is the dependency LEAF: the whole deploy effect as a pure, injectable, OFFLINE-testable service. NO command kind, NO vocabulary edit, NO registry edit, NO roster backfill - all of that is the parent.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-fa3a3e17:
- `git grep -c "deployment\\.deploy|deployment\\.set_target" -- apps packages tests` = 0. No deployment surface exists. The gap is real.
- THE PATTERN TO MIRROR IS `repository.publish`, and it is small: `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/node-publisher.ts` is 77 lines (`NodePublisherConfig:20`, `PublishReport:29`, `createNodePublisher:35`) - a thin effect runner, not a framework.
- THE RECEIPT SHAPE IS `apps/daemon/src/repository/publish-receipt-contracts.ts`: `PUBLISH_RECEIPT_VERSION = "moe-publish-receipt/1"` (:16), `PUBLISH_RECEIPT_COMMAND_KIND = "internal.repository.publish_receipt"` (:17), `PublishRefusal` (:36), `PublishReceiptV1` (:41), and a decode-result union (:57). Mirror it.
- INTERNAL RECEIPT KINDS NEED NO ROSTER BACKFILL. `grep -n "internal\\." apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` returns ZERO - `internal.*` receipt kinds are outside PAYLOAD_KEYS, the registry and the MCP roster entirely. That is what lets this row own `moe-deploy-receipt/1` without touching a roster. Confirm it before writing the receipt; if it has changed, STOP rather than absorbing a backfill.

THE PREVIOUS RECEIPT'S SHAPE IS THIS ROW'S MOST CONSEQUENTIAL OUTPUT. The monitoring/rollback row (task-7683a432eb3f4e87b1eb0cbc6e3a55ff) rolls back to it and is a SIBLING that cannot depend on this row - so it will build against whatever ships. Get the shape right the first time.

ATOMIC REPLACE IS THE PROPERTY THAT MATTERS. A deploy that stops the old container before the new one is healthy produces a window where the product is down and the operator sees an outage they did not cause.
definitionOfDone: The deploy effect is tested OFFLINE through injectable docker/ssh ports that capture argv, asserting the ARGV BYTE-FOR-BYTE: the build tag EQUALS the landed sha, and the ssh path is `docker save | ssh docker load`. A tag that is not the sha makes every later rollback, dossier and incident claim unverifiable, so assert the tag against the sha value rather than against a pattern. No test may reach the network or a real docker daemon.

ATOMIC REPLACE PROVEN, not asserted in prose: through the port's recorded call ORDER, assert the OLD container still serves until the NEW one answers health, and that there is NO point in the sequence at which neither serves. Mutate the service to a stop-then-start order and confirm the arm goes RED - an ordering property that has never been seen red is not evidence.

DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT REFUSES and leaves the environment in a DEFINED state - the old container still running - asserted with code AND layer, and asserted by reading the port's final state rather than by trusting the return value. A half-deployed environment reporting success is worse than a refusal.

DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING, DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED and DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE each assert code AND layer. DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED carries the tool's ACTUAL last stderr line, not a generic message - assert the real stderr text reaches the refusal, since a generic build failure is undiagnosable from a receipt.

`moe-deploy-receipt/1` records {environment, sha, imageDigest, url, DEPLOYED|REFUSED(code)}, mirroring apps/daemon/src/repository/publish-receipt-contracts.ts including its null-pairing discipline (exactly one of the success member and the refusal member populated). A REFUSED receipt carries its code and no imageDigest, asserted as its own arm.

THE PREVIOUS RECEIPT IS KEPT AND READABLE: assert that two successive deploys leave BOTH receipts retrievable and distinguishable by sha. The rollback row task-7683a432eb3f4e87b1eb0cbc6e3a55ff is a sibling that cannot depend on this one and will build against this shape, so document the retrieval call it should use in the completion record.

A PRODUCTION deploy CITES the release decision when one exists on the goal and states 'no release decision' when none does - assert BOTH wordings. It neither invents an approval nor refuses for lack of one. The decision is read through an injectable port; this row does not implement Gate 3 (task-2a345b2e97d94599b4688af1923056e5, a sibling).

EVERY container, temp directory and child process the tests create is released on EVERY exit path including the throwing one (epic rail 4) - teardown in a `finally`, not after the assertions. Invoke `docker`/`ssh` as bare executables under shell:false with argv arrays; never a hard-coded `.cmd`, never a shell string, never a chain. Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: NO COMMAND KIND. No edit to daemon-command-vocabulary.ts, daemon-command-registry.ts, mcp-tool-allowlist.ts, agent-spawn-contract.ts or packages/contracts - every one belongs to the parent task-04b3ce7e349743c2a156d32ee5550ba5 and touching them here collides in the shared worktree.
ATOMIC REPLACE: the old container serves until the new one is healthy. A stop-then-start deploy is an outage the operator did not ask for.
THE IMAGE TAG IS THE LANDED SHA. Every later claim - rollback, dossier, incident - resolves through it.
KEEP THE PREVIOUS RECEIPT and get its shape right first time: the rollback row is a SIBLING that cannot depend on this row, so it will build against whatever ships.
FOLLOW `repository.publish`'s pattern (node-publisher.ts, publish-receipt-contracts.ts). A second deployment shape is a second thing to reason about during an incident.
OFFLINE TESTS ONLY. Every port is injectable; no test may reach the network or a real docker daemon. A test that leaks a container or a port makes every later gate on this board inadmissible.

FIND IT in what 3706b7e7 shipped and build the switch on THAT. If the generated infrastructure has NO switch point, DoD-2 is unsatisfiable as written and the correct output is STOP AND REPORT with the compose file quoted - not a stop-then-start deploy described as atomic, and not a proxy invented here (that is 3706b7e7's file to change). (c) READ THE THREE FILES YOU ARE MIRRORING, all small and all deliberate: `orchestrator/node-publisher.ts` (77 lines - a thin effect runner, not a framework), `repository/publish-receipt-contracts.ts` (185), `repository/publish-ledger.ts` (246, whose `readPublishLedger(store, projectId)` at :84 and `recordPublishReceipt` at :195 are the retrieval and record shapes DoD-6 asks you to mirror and document). `repository/git-landing-port.ts` (243) is the injectable-port precedent: `GitRunner = (cwd, args, stdin?) => Promise<{code, stderr, stdout}>` - copy that shape rather than inventing one. (e) `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src` and note peer dirt; never revert it.

implementationPlan.description: THE RECEIPT CONTRACT. NEW FILE `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-receipt-contracts.ts` (target <=250 lines; the file it mirrors is 185). Mirror `publish-receipt-contracts.ts` in SHAPE, not by copy-paste - read it and follow its decisions. Declare `DEPLOY_RECEIPT_VERSION = "moe-deploy-receipt/1"`, `DEPLOY_RECEIPT_COMMAND_KIND = "internal.deployment.deploy_receipt"` (the `internal.*` prefix is what keeps this off every roster - see step 1a), a reserved principal id beside `NODE_PUBLISHER_PRINCIPAL_ID`, the four refusal codes, and `DeployReceiptV1` carrying {environment, sha, imageDigest, url, outcome} plus the record-keeping members its sibling carries (decidedAt, projectId, receiptId, version). THE NULL-PAIRING DISCIPLINE IS THE POINT (DoD-5): `PublishReceiptV1` pairs `outcome: "PUSHED" | "REFUSED"` with `sha: string | null`, `branch: string | null`, `url: string | null` and `refusal: PublishRefusal | null`, and EXACTLY ONE side is populated. Carry that literally: a DEPLOYED receipt has an imageDigest and a null refusal; a REFUSED receipt has its code and a NULL imageDigest. Encode it as an exact-key decode with a validator that REFUSES a receipt with both populated or neither - a shape that merely allows nulls on both sides is not the discipline, it is the absence of one. Include the decode-result union (`{ok: true, receipt} | {code: "DEPLOY_RECEIPT_INVALID", ok: false}`) and validate the sha with the same anchored hex pattern its sibling uses for git object ids - a tag that is not a sha is the failure DoD-1 exists to prevent, and catching it at decode is cheaper than at rollback.

THE PORTS, AND THE TEST DOUBLE THAT CAN ACTUALLY PROVE DoD-2. NEW FILE `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-ports.ts`. Follow `GitRunner`: `(args: readonly string[], stdin?) => Promise<{code, stderr, stdout}>` for docker and for ssh, with a timeout and a bounded output tail (git-landing-port.ts uses `GIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000`, `MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES = 8MB`, `DETAIL_TAIL = 600` - deploys are slower than pushes, so pick your own and SAY WHY rather than copying 60 s unexamined). SPAWN DISCIPLINE, and it is a rail: bare executable `docker` / `ssh` under `shell: false` with an ARGV ARRAY - never a hard-coded `.cmd`, never a shell string, never a chain. `moe-up-spawn.ts:103-111` states `shell: false` explicitly rather than relying on the default and says why; do the same. THE `docker save | ssh docker load` PIPE IS THE ONE PLACE THIS GETS SUBTLE (DoD-1): a pipe is a shell construct, and you may not use a shell. Wire the two children's streams in Node - `save`'s stdout to `ssh`'s stdin - and assert BOTH argv arrays independently. Say in the step note how you connected them and how a failure in EITHER child is surfaced, because a pipe hides the first process's exit code by default (`${PIPESTATUS[0]}` is the shell answer and you have no shell). NOW THE TEST DOUBLE, and this is the design decision that decides whether DoD-2 is provable: A PURE ARGV RECORDER CANNOT ANSWER "was there a point at which neither container served". Recording calls in order tells you what was invoked, not what was RUNNING. So the double must be a SMALL STATE MACHINE: it tracks each container as started/healthy/stopped as the recorded argv would have moved it, and exposes that state for assertion. DoD-3 says so directly - "asserted by reading the port's final state rather than by trusting the return value". Build that state model here, beside the port it doubles, so the service's tests and any later row's tests share ONE model of what docker did.

THE ENGINE. NEW FILE `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-service.ts` (target <=250 lines). `node-publisher.ts` is 77 lines and the rail says follow it: a THIN effect runner, not a framework. Nothing here chooses a moment or a policy - the caller names the environment and the sha, the ports do the work, one receipt is recorded per deploy. THE SEQUENCE, and its order IS the atomicity property: build the image tagged with the LANDED SHA (DoD-1: the tag EQUALS the sha value, not a pattern that matches one); transfer it if the target is remote (`docker save | ssh docker load`); start the NEW container alongside the old; probe health until it answers or the budget expires; ONLY THEN flip at the switch point step 1(b) identified; and only after the flip stop the old container. FOUR REFUSALS, each with code AND layer (DoD-4): DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING, DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED, DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE, DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT. DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED CARRIES THE TOOL'S ACTUAL LAST STDERR LINE, not a generic message - `git-landing-port.ts` clips git's own words into `detail` with `DETAIL_TAIL`, and the reason is the same: a generic build failure is undiagnosable from a receipt weeks later. ON DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT THE OLD CONTAINER KEEPS RUNNING AND THE NEW ONE IS REMOVED (DoD-3): a refusal must leave a DEFINED state, and the tidy-up of the failed candidate belongs on the failure path, in a `finally`, not after the assertions. THE RELEASE-DECISION READ (DoD-7) IS AN INJECTABLE PORT AND NOTHING MORE: for a PRODUCTION deploy, cite the release decision when the port answers one and state 'no release decision' when it does not. It neither invents an approval nor refuses for the lack of one - Gate 3 is task-2a345b2e, a sibling, and implementing a gate here would be inventing authority. Record the receipt through a ledger module mirroring `recordPublishReceipt`/`readPublishLedger`; DoD-6 asks you to NAME the retrieval call in the completion record, because the rollback row task-7683a432 is a sibling that cannot depend on this one and will build against whatever ships.

THE TESTS, OFFLINE, WITH THE ORDERING ARM FIRST. New test files beside their modules. NO TEST MAY REACH THE NETWORK OR A REAL DOCKER DAEMON (rail 6) - every port is the double from step 3. (1) DoD-2, THE ATOMICITY ARM, and it is the row's most valuable artifact: drive a deploy through the state-machine double and assert that at EVERY step of the recorded sequence at least one container was serving - walk the recorded transitions and assert the invariant over all of them, rather than checking the two endpoints, because a stop-then-start deploy has correct endpoints and a hole in the middle. That is exactly the shape a naive arm misses. (2) DoD-1: the build argv BYTE-FOR-BYTE with the tag EQUAL to the sha value under test (not `toMatch(/[0-9a-f]{40}/)` - a pattern passes for the WRONG sha, and every later rollback and incident claim resolves through this tag), and both argv arrays of the `save | ssh load` path. (3) DoD-3: health timeout refuses with code AND layer, and the double's FINAL STATE shows the old container running and the candidate removed. (4) DoD-4: the other three refusals with code AND layer, and DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED carrying a distinctive stderr string planted in the double - assert that exact text reaches the refusal, so a generic message cannot pass. (5) DoD-5: a DEPLOYED receipt round-trips with an imageDigest and null refusal; a REFUSED receipt carries its code and a NULL imageDigest; and a hand-built receipt with BOTH populated is REFUSED by the decoder - that third arm is the null-pairing discipline, without it the shape merely permits nulls. (6) DoD-6: two successive deploys leave BOTH receipts retrievable and distinguishable BY SHA. (7) DoD-7: both wordings - a production deploy citing a release decision, and one stating 'no release decision' - asserted on the receipt or report text. (8) EPIC RAIL 4, and it applies to the tests themselves: every temp directory and child the tests create is released on EVERY exit path INCLUDING THE THROWING ONE - teardown in `finally`, never after the assertions.

DRILLS, GATES, SELF-REVIEW. (a) DRILLS, recorded in the step note. `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths FIRST. EVERY FILE THIS ROW CREATES IS NEW AND UNTRACKED (`??`), so global rail 13 fires in full and `git diff` is BLIND to all of them - empty before, during and after. Back each up out of tree (%TEMP%, suffixed by worker id) and prove restoration by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore; a copy can silently no-op and "the command returned" is not evidence the bytes moved. State that no tracked path was mutated. THREE DRILLS: (i) DoD-2's, named in the DoD itself and the one that decides whether the atomicity arm is real - change the service to STOP THE OLD CONTAINER BEFORE STARTING THE NEW and confirm the ordering arm goes RED, quoting the failing transition. An ordering property that has never been seen red is not evidence. (ii) Change the build tag from the sha to any other value and confirm the DoD-1 arm reds NAMING the expected sha - if it stays green the assertion was a pattern, not a value. (iii) Populate both the imageDigest and the refusal on one receipt and confirm the decoder refuses - if it passes, the null-pairing discipline was not encoded. (b) GATES - standalone foreground, one command per call, no pipes and no `;` chains, quoting each `Test Files N passed` count line; an exit-0 leg with no count line ran nothing: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` is NOT evidence for this row - vitest.config.ts:32 includes no `apps/**`, so it runs zero tests against every file here. Attribute red by failing paths at HEAD minus the step-1 baseline, intersected with this row's owned paths; that intersection must be EMPTY. (c) ADVERSARIAL PASS on this diff only: a health probe that answers 200 on the OLD container while the new one is still starting (does the probe address the candidate specifically, or could it pass by reading the thing it is replacing - this is the subtlest bug available here); a deploy of the SAME sha twice (idempotent, or a second receipt); the switch flip succeeding and the old-container stop FAILING - what state is recorded; a `docker save` that fails after `ssh` has already started; an environment name or url with a shell metacharacter (you use no shell - confirm that is actually true of every call site); any container, temp dir or child left alive on a throwing path. (d) COMPLETION RECORD must state: THE SWITCH POINT you built the atomic flip on and where task-3706b7e7 defines it - or, if it defines none, that DoD-2 was reported rather than approximated; the exact retrieval call the rollback row task-7683a432 should use for the previous receipt, with its signature (DoD-6 asks for this by name and that row cannot depend on this one); the health-probe budget you chose and why it differs from git's 60 s; drill (i) verbatim; and that no command kind, vocabulary, registry or roster file was touched - `git status --porcelain` proves it.

comments.author: architect-b63fabf3
comments.content:
TWO THINGS THIS ROW LEFT UNSETTLED THAT WOULD SURFACE MID-STEP. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 6 steps, 6 files, all new.

Both of the row's measured claims re-confirmed at plan time: the deployment gap is real (`git grep -c` = 0), and `grep -c 'internal\.' daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` = **0**, so `internal.*` receipt kinds really are outside PAYLOAD_KEYS, the registry and the MCP roster. `moe-deploy-receipt/1` costs no backfill — same mechanism `SEAT_EXIT_COMMAND_KIND` uses.

## 1. DoD-2 may be unbuildable on what the sibling shipped

"Atomic replace" needs something *flippable*, and **bare docker gives you none** — you cannot re-publish a port on a running container. So "start new, probe health, flip" requires a reverse-proxy upstream, a compose service alias, or equivalent — and that switch point is defined by what **task-3706b7e7 generates**, not by this row.

Step 1 therefore makes the worker read what that row actually shipped *before* designing the flip, and makes "the generated infrastructure defines no switch point" a **stop-and-report** — with the compose file quoted. The two outcomes to refuse are shipping a stop-then-start deploy described as atomic, and inventing a proxy inside another row's generated files (rail 1 forbids reaching across).

## 2. An argv recorder cannot prove atomicity

DoD-2 asks whether there was *any point at which neither container served*. A recorder answers "what was invoked, in what order" — not what was **running**. So the test double must be a **small state machine** tracking each container as started/healthy/stopped. DoD-3 already implies it ("assert by reading the port's final state rather than by trusting the return value"); the plan makes it explicit and puts it beside the port, so the service tests and any later row share one model of what docker did.

And the arm must **walk every transition**, not check the endpoints: a stop-then-start deploy has correct endpoints and a hole in the middle — precisely what a naive arm misses.

## The subtlest bug available here, named in the adversarial pass

**A health probe that addresses the environment's public URL rather than the candidate container** answers 200 from the *old* container while the new one is still starting. Every deploy then "passes" health instantly, and DoD-2 and DoD-3 are both vacuous while green.

## Three smaller findings carried into the plan

- **The `docker save | ssh docker load` pipe is a shell construct and there is no shell.** The streams join in Node, and a pipe hides the first child's exit code by default — `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` is the shell answer and unavailable here. Both argv arrays asserted independently, both children's failures surfaced.
- **`toMatch(/[0-9a-f]{40}/)` passes for the wrong sha.** DoD-1 says the tag *equals* the sha value; every later rollback and incident claim resolves through it. Drill (ii) proves the assertion is a value, not a pattern.
- **Null-pairing is a validator, not a type.** `T | null` on both sides merely *permits* the pairing; the discipline is a decoder that refuses both-populated and neither-populated. Drill (iii) proves it was encoded.

## The output that outlives this row

DoD-6's retrieval call. `task-7683a432` (rollback) is a **sibling that cannot depend on this row** and will build against whatever ships — so the completion record must name the call and its signature, mirroring `readPublishLedger(store, projectId)` / `recordPublishReceipt`. That is a deliverable, not a formality.

The two failure modes to refuse are shipping a stop-then-start deploy described as atomic, and inventing a proxy inside another row's generated files.

SECOND - AN ARGV RECORDER CANNOT PROVE ATOMICITY. It records what was invoked, not what was running. Without a state-machine double the atomicity arm is a prose claim with a test-shaped wrapper. And asserting only the endpoints of the sequence passes a stop-then-start deploy, which has correct endpoints and a hole in the middle - walk every transition.

THIRD - `toMatch(/[0-9a-f]{40}/)` PASSES FOR THE WRONG SHA. DoD-1 says the tag EQUALS the sha value; every later rollback, dossier and incident claim resolves through that tag. Drill (ii) is what proves the assertion is a value and not a pattern.

FOURTH - THE PIPE IS A SHELL CONSTRUCT AND THERE IS NO SHELL. `docker save | ssh docker load` must be joined in Node, and a pipe hides the first child's exit code by default - `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` is the shell answer and unavailable here. Surface BOTH children's failures, and assert both argv arrays independently.

FIFTH - THE HEALTH PROBE COULD READ THE CONTAINER IT IS REPLACING. If the probe addresses the environment's public url rather than the candidate specifically, it answers 200 from the OLD container and every deploy "passes" health instantly - the subtlest bug available in this row, and it would make DoD-2 and DoD-3 both vacuous while green. The adversarial pass names it.

SIXTH - A REFUSAL MUST LEAVE A DEFINED STATE. On DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT the old container keeps running AND the failed candidate is removed - the tidy-up belongs on the failure path in a `finally`. A half-deployed environment reporting success is worse than a refusal, and so is one reporting a refusal while leaving a stray container.

SEVENTH - THE RECEIPT SHAPE IS THIS ROW'S MOST CONSEQUENTIAL OUTPUT. The rollback row task-7683a432 is a SIBLING that cannot depend on this one and will build against whatever ships. DoD-6 asks for the retrieval call to be NAMED in the completion record; treat that as the deliverable it is, not a formality.

EIGHTH - NULL-PAIRING IS A VALIDATOR, NOT A TYPE. `T | null` on both sides merely PERMITS the pairing; the discipline is a decoder that REFUSES both-populated and neither-populated. Drill (iii) proves it was encoded.
